questions.body: Which is a major advantage of the use of rubidium-82 (Rb-82) over nitrogen-13-ammonia (N-13 ammonia)?

A minor spill of Rb-82 chloride (half-life of 76 seconds) is identified on the patient table of a PET/CT scanner before a study. What is the most appropriate approach to handle the contamination before the next scan?
22 11 Na (sodium 22, 11 neutrons, and 11 protons decay). Using conservation of charge and nucleon number (neglect neutrino emissions), which decay scheme would be allowed?

A small outpatient PET/CT laboratory is transitioning from using 10 patients a day using rubidium-82 (Rb-82) generators for cardiac imaging to 10 patients a day using F-18-labeled radiopharmaceuticals. The imaging suite has a nearby patient waiting room adjacent to the injection and hot lab areas. Which of the following best describes the primary shielding consideration that should be addressed during this transition?

In October 2024, the delayed restart of a nuclear reactor in the Netherlands caused supply shortages of several imaging radiopharmaceuticals. Which of the following imaging agents was affected by the reactor shutdown?
Which instrument is the most suitable for performing ambient exposure rate surveys of radioactive material work areas? (Readouts in parenthesis)

The average person in the United States receives approximately how much dose annually from natural background sources of radiation (includes radon, cosmic rays, and internal radionuclides; excludes medical exposures)?
Geiger-Müller survey meters operate at which region of the voltage-response curve shown here?

A positron emitted from a PET radiotracer annihilates with an electron, producing two 511 keV photons traveling in nearly opposite directions. Before reaching the detector, one of these photons undergoes Compton scattering at a 90° angle, reducing its energy to approximately 255 keV. The other photon is detected at 511 keV. The PET scanner operates with an energy window of 400–600 keV. How will the PET system handle this event?

A technologist localizes a contaminated area in the nuclear cardiology department using a Geiger-Müller survey meter. A wipe test of the area should then be performed to identify the radionuclide. Which instrument is most appropriate for assessing the wipe sample?
A nursing mother presents for a Tc-99m sestamibi myocardial perfusion study. What is the recommended duration of breastfeeding interruption?

For a technetium-99m (Tc-99m) source, the Half-Value Layer (HVL) of lead is 0.4 mm at 140 keV. How many HVLs are required to reduce the exposure to 1/8 of its initial value, and what is the corresponding total thickness of lead?
Which practice is the most effective for keeping staff occupational exposure As Low As Reasonably Achievable (ALARA)?
Which number refers to the number of nucleons in this atom?
Rubidium-82 (Rb-82) has a higher emitted positron energy than N-13 ammonia; therefore, which of the following is correct?
Deterministic radiation effects include which of the following?
What is the primary advantage of iterative reconstruction over filtered backprojection?

Consider the uptake characteristics of two flow tracers below. An ischemic defect is imaged with Tracer A . The patient returns and is imaged with Tracer B . If there is no change in the patient's underlying blood flow, how do the different uptake characteristics alter the intensity of the ischemic defect?
Dose calibrator constancy testing is performed daily. How often must dose calibrator geometry testing be performed?
Nuclei that lie above the Valley of Stability have an excess of protons relative to neutrons. What is/are mechanism(s) for achieving greater stability?
Physical collimation is used in SPECT but not needed in PET because of which of the following?
Which of the following constitutes a reportable medical event under NRC regulations?
Which of the following radiopharmaceuticals has linear myocardial uptake and blood flow relationship?

A patient undergoes a same-day exercise flurpiridaz F-18 PET myocardial perfusion study. The patient receives a 2.5 mCi-rest dose followed by a 9.0 mCi-exercise stress dose. Immediately after the stress acquisition begins, the PET scanner experiences a hardware failure and the study is aborted. The patient has already completed the exercise portion of the examination. Once the scanner is operational again, when may the patient be reimaged?
A non-circular orbit is preferred for SPECT cardiac imaging with parallel hole collimators because of which of the following?
Which of the following is a characteristic of time-of-flight PET imaging compared to traditional PET?
Digital PET (use of silicon photomultipliers) does which of the following?
A controlled area has an ambient exposure rate of 7.5 mrem/h. What sign should be posted on all the entrance door(s)?
Which of the following are the acceptable NRC limits of strontium-82 (Sr-82) and Sr-85 in a rubidium-82 (Rb-82) patient injection?
If the exposure rate at 3 m from a radioactive source is 100 mR/h, what will be the exposure rate at 6 m?
A technologist increases the mAs (milliampere-seconds) of a cardiac CT study. What is the impact on the resulting CT images?
Radioactive syringes ( unit dose ) received from a radiopharmacy should be measured with which of the following instruments prior to patient administration?
Which SPECT imaging isotope will show the best photopeak energy resolution (smallest %FWHM)?
Which of the following units is a measure of absorbed dose?
Which of the following describes flurpiridaz F-18 uptake mechanism for myocardial perfusion imaging?
A package containing radioactive material has a measured exposure rate of 100 mrem/h at the surface and 1.6 mrem/h at 1 meter. What is the appropriate label and Transport Index (TI) for this package?

A laboratory transitions from Rb-82 PET myocardial perfusion imaging to flurpiridaz F-18 PET. Flurpiridaz has a higher myocardial extraction fraction than Rb-82. A patient with stable coronary artery disease undergoes repeat imaging with flurpiridaz after previously being imaged with Rb-82. Assuming no change in the patient's coronary disease, how should the perfusion defects appear on the flurpiridaz images?
For a gamma camera with parallel-hole collimation, as object distance increases, which of the following is correct?
The annual whole-body occupational dose to radiation workers is limited to ________ per year.
Molybdenum breakthrough testing is routinely performed in a nuclear pharmacy using which of the following?
Which of the following statements is true regarding the transient equilibrium of a molybdenum-99 (Mo-99)/technetium-99 (Tc-99m) generator?

An F-18-labelled perfusion agent (t 1/2 = 110 minutes) is injected with 3 mCi at t = 0. A protocol calls for the dose to decay by a factor of 8 before a second PET dose can be administered. How long must the lab wait before injecting the second dose?
A key advantage of iterative reconstruction versus filtered backprojection (FBP) is which of the following?
A laboratory performs a flurpiridaz F-18 PET study using a standard Tc-99m syringe shield because a PET-rated syringe shield is unavailable. Which statement is most accurate?

Area surveys are to be performed with a survey meter sufficiently sensitive to detect 0.1 mR/hr in areas where radioactive materials are prepared and administered. How often must this survey be performed in the Nuclear Cardiology rooms?

A patient is imaged on a SPECT/CT hybrid system for cardiac perfusion assessment. During the procedure, the patient shifts approximately 1 cm to the left between the transmission (CT attenuation map) acquisition and the emission (SPECT) scan. What is the most appropriate course of action to manage this situation?
The radiochemical purity of a technetium-99 radiopharmaceutical is established by which of the following?

A nuclear cardiology technologist declares her pregnancy in writing to the Radiation Safety Officer. Upon investigation, it is determined that the dose to the embryo/fetus was 100 mrem at the time of declaration. How much longer can the technologist work in the radioactive materials environment?
Which of the following is considered a best practice for minimizing radiation dose in cardiac SPECT imaging?
The presence of molybdenum-99 (Mo-99) in a Mo-99/Tc-99m eluate is an example of which of the following?
What is the primary purpose of daily intrinsic or extrinsic uniformity testing?
A 4-quadrant bar phantom shows smallest resolvable bars of 3.5 mm. What is the approximate full width at half maximum (FWHM)?
What is the best solution to manage image noise?

A 53-year-old woman with a history of morbid obesity (BMI 41 Kg/m 2 ), type II diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and sleep apnea is undergoing an evaluation for bariatric surgery. She has no chest pain, but she is limited by dyspnea and fatigue with less than 1 block of walking. Her ECG is normal, except for low-voltage QRS. You decided to perform Tc-99m SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging for evaluation for ischemic heart disease. Which study protocol will you recommend for this patient?

A 43-year-old female with a history of treated hypertension presented with non-exertional, left-sided, sharp, fleeting chest pain, lasting 1 to 2 seconds. The ECG is normal. Her exercise tolerance is not restricted. According to the 2023 Multimodality Appropriate Use Criteria for the detection and risk assessment of chronic coronary disease, which of the following studies represents an appropriate next step?
Failure to apply an adequate overall flood-field uniformity correction is seen most strikingly as ______ on transverse images of the uniform section of a SPECT Performance Phantom.
Which of the following left ventricular volumes curves (A–D) would be encountered in a patient with a restrictive hypertensive cardiomyopathy?

Although differentiation of ischemic versus non-ischemic cardiomyopathy with gated myocardial perfusion SPECT may be challenging, a clue to the presence of an ischemic cardiomyopathy is which of the following?

In gated myocardial perfusion SPECT images performed on a hypertensive elderly female, 5' 6”, 130 lbs, status post (S/P) left mastectomy, an extensive mildly/moderately fixed lateral perfusion defect is observed with associated normal regional wall motion and systolic wall thickening. LVEF = 68%. The most likely explanation for the lateral perfusion defect is which of the following?
Which of the following will MOST improve myocardial perfusion SPECT specificity in detecting coronary artery disease?
Left ventricular filling due to the left atrial kick is best evaluated by which of the following radionuclide techniques?
Attenuation correction of myocardial perfusion SPECT can be performed with which of the following external radionuclide sources?
The Ramp filter, employed with filtered backprojection, is most likely to result in a myocardial perfusion artifact under which of the following circumstances?
Respiratory gating of myocardial perfusion SPECT acquisitions has been investigated and has been demonstrated to be useful to which of the following:
Which of the following agents should not be used for pharmacologic stress in a patient with left bundle branch block (LBBB)?
The Society of Motion Picture and Television Engineers (SMPTE) pattern testing evaluates which of the following?

Gut activity can affect the quality of the images making them difficult to interpret. Several methods have been used to improve the quality of the images. Which of the following is the best method to alleviate gut interference/artifact?

In reconstructed SPECT myocardial perfusion images, the left ventricular cavity appears “oblong” rather than round, and there appear to be opposed inferoseptal and anterolateral perfusion defects. To investigate potential artifact as a cause of this finding in three consecutive patients, which of the following should you do?
Compared to gated blood pool SPECT, planar equilibrium radionuclide ventriculography provides which of the following advantages?
The left ventricular endocardial border of a myocardial perfusion SPECT scan will be less well resolved using which of the following acquisition/processing modifications?
Which of the following left ventricular volumes curves (A-D) would be encountered in a patient with atrial fibrillation and a heart rate of approximately 75 bpm?
Which of the following myocardial perfusion SPECT processing methods will most likely underestimate perfusion defect extent and severity?
Which of the following is TRUE regarding stress-only SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging?

A 74-year-old man with past medical history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, obesity (BMI = 33 Kg/m 2 ), old myocardial infarction, and status post CABG 7 years ago. He presented with new-onset dyspnea on exertion for the past 3 months. ECG shows normal sinus rhythm with inferior Q-waves. You decided to refer the patient for exercise stress Tc-99m SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging. You have a conventional A-SPECT camera with CT attenuation correction capability. Which study protocol will you recommend for this patient?
What is a typical range of X-ray tube current and tube potential settings for attenuation correction on a hybrid SPECT/CT system?
Which of the following is considered “Alert Limits” during daily quality-control testing and patient infusions?

A 48-year-old man with a history of controlled hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus is referred for evaluation of new-onset epigastric pain. His exercise tolerance is unrestricted, his BMI is 31 Kg/m2, and his ECG is normal. You decided to refer the patient for Tc-99m SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging. You have a conventional A-SPECT camera with CT attenuation correction. Which study protocol will you recommend for this patient?
Which one of the following QC procedures for a SPECT system is considered optional?

The following rest/stress MPI protocol is used routinely in a laboratory: 10 mCi/30 mCi Tc-99m tetrofosmin 45-min post-injection rest-and-stress supine SPECT 180° 45° RAO to 45° LPO acquisitions 15-min rest/12-min post-stress acquisition times For obese patients the same protocol is used, but the rest/stress activities are increased to 12 mCi and 36 mCi, respectively, in order to increase myocardial count density. To achieve a similar increase in myocardial count density, what other protocol modification could be made?

Which of the following artifactual myocardial perfusion patterns is most frequently associated with horizontal (x-direction) patient motion during SPECT acquisition? The blackened regions represent perfusion defects.

A 55-year-old male presents with chest pain and exertional dyspnea. Based upon the findings in the rest/stress myocardial perfusion scan below, which of the following would be an appropriate next step in patient management?
Which of the following scenarios constitutes an appropriate use of stress myocardial perfusion imaging in a symptomatic patient following a coronary CT angiography (CCTA)?

A patient with hyperkalemia undergoes gated myocardial perfusion SPECT. Of the accepted cardiac cycles, 70% are correctly gated on the electrocardiographic R-wave, and 30% are incorrectly gated on a tall T-wave. What will be the most likely effect on the calculated left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF)?
What is the recommended activity of a point source for Center of Rotation (COR) acquisition?

In a rest/stress Tc-9m sestamibi SPECT scan a small, fixed focus of moderately/markedly decreased radiotracer concentration is noted in the very apex of the left ventricle. Normal apical regional wall motion and systolic wall thickening are present. This finding is most likely due to which of the following:
A gated MPI study shows EF = 25%, but raw cine demonstrates flashing with irregular R-R intervals. What is the most likely cause?
Which of the following scenarios constitutes a “rarely appropriate” use of stress myocardial perfusion imaging in a patient with chest pain?
Acquiring the prone position on a SPECT MPI is helpful to alleviate the following image artifacts, except which of the following?

According to the 2023 Multimodality Appropriate Use Criteria for the detection and risk assessment of chronic coronary disease, which of the following scenarios represents an “Appropriate” use of stress SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging among asymptomatic patients with known coronary disease and prior revascularization?
Which of the following photon energy windows will yield the lowest count density technetium-99m (Tc-99m) tetrofosmin myocardial perfusion SPECT scan?
How frequently should Geometry testing be performed for Dose Calibrator quality control?
What is the main advantage of iterative reconstruction compared to filtered backprojection?

In the planar projection images of a Tc-99m sestamibi myocardial perfusion SPECT scan a moderately intense focus of radiotracer concentration is noted in the patient's left axilla in both the rest and post-stress acquisitions. This most likely represents which of the following:
In iterative reconstruction algorithms, ordered subsets expectation maximization (OSEM) differs from maximum likelihood expectation maximization (MLEM) due to which of the following?
Which of the following represents an “Appropriate” use of stress myocardial perfusion imaging in patients with no ischemic equivalent symptoms?
Flood-field uniformity should be checked daily for which of the following:
How often must a survey meter be calibrated?
Which of the following electrocardiographic findings is most likely to adversely affect ECG gating during myocardial perfusion imaging?
Which of the following is considered the Expiration Limits during daily quality-control testing and patient infusions?
How do the reconstructed images differ between 180° vs 360° acquisition in SPECT MPI?

A 48-year-old female with hypertension develops chest pain with exertion or with sitting for a prolonged period of time. She undergoes exercise stress electrocardiography, which is equivocal. She is referred for exercise stress SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging. On arrival to the lab, she has a baseline blood pressure of 128/74mmHg, heart rate of 84, and LBBB on her presenting ECG (new since prior). She exercises for 11 minutes with reproduction of her chest pain and has an appropriate hemodynamic response. Her perfusion images are shown below. Gated images show normal function. What is the most likely interpretation of this study?

You are evaluating the statistical characteristics of a cardiovascular test. Of 50 patients with the disease, 40 test positive and 10 test negative. Of 50 patients without the disease, 45 test negative and 5 test positive. What is the sensitivity of the test, and is it affected by the prevalence of the disease?
Which of the following parameters are most affected early in the course of amyloid cardiomyopathy compared to normal subjects?
Select the best answer for the intervention(s) shown to improve PFR and TPFR:
Which patient has an “appropriate” indication for exercise SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI)?

A 64-year-old patient with angina presents to clinic for further evaluation. The patient has a history of CAD with PCI to the LAD approximately 1 year ago, in the setting of NSTEMI. No other coronary stenoses of concern were seen. Hypertension is controlled on candesartan and amlodipine. Impaired glucose is managed with metformin. Technetium-99m SPECT is performed with images as shown below. LVEF is 51% on stress images and 62% on rest images. Amlodipine is increased for angina. Which of the following statements is correct?

A 65-year-old male with known CAD and LVEF of 30% is referred for SPECT viability testing prior to planned revascularization. He has a 70% mid to distal left anterior descending (LAD) stenosis, chronic total obstruction (CTO) of the proximal right coronary artery (RCA), and non-obstructive disease in the left circumflex artery (LCX). There are collaterals from the LCX and LAD to the RCA. Rest, 4-hour redistribution, and 24-hour redistribution Tl-201 SPECT images are shown. Which of the following is the best course of action based on these findings?

A 62-year-old female presents for stress SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging. She is in the emergency department with exertional chest pain with recent concerning CT coronary angiography that 2 weeks earlier revealed a 50% to 69% mid-LAD lesion with CT-FFR not performed. She has a history of sick sinus syndrome s/p pacemaker programmed in DDD mode, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, aortic stenosis, and coronary artery disease. She had a recent echocardiogram that revealed intact left ventricular function, basal septal hypertrophy with a 34 mmHg resting gradient, and moderate aortic stenosis. Her ED workup included no concerning ECG changes and 2 negative troponins. Her resting ECG on arrival to the stress lab revealed atrial pacing with a narrow QRS. Which of the following is a contraindication for exercise stress and indication for vasodilator stress?
Which of the following is NOT assessed by the uptake of SPECT myocardial viability tracers (ie, Tl-201)?
Which of the following is an absolute criterion for early cessation of an exercise stress test?

While processing a planar MUGA (ERNA) study, a cardiology trainee selects a single end-diastolic region of interest (ROI) for calculation of LVEF. If the ROI for background subtraction is placed over an enlarged, hot spleen rather than the normal paraventricular region, how will the LVEF calculation be affected?

A 74-year-old male is referred for pharmacologic stress MPI for exertional shortness of breath and in preparation for an upcoming Whipple procedure. These perfusion images and associated polar plots were generated. Semi-quantitative analysis of the images was performed to help inform decision-making, including generation of the summed stress score (SSS), summed rest score (SRS), and percentage LV ischemia (%LVIsch). What is the calculated summed stress score and %LV Ischemia?

When reporting on extra-cardiac findings on a stress PET/CT study, a pulmonary nodule is found. Which one of the following is not considered a risk factor for malignancy when utilizing the Fleischner Society Guidelines?

A 42-year-old female is undergoing a SPECT/CT myocardial perfusion imaging for pre-op testing prior to renal transplant for autosomal dominant polycystic renal disease. The following is seen on the attenuation CT review. Which of the following are your next best steps?

A 58-year-old woman with diabetes mellitus and obesity is evaluated for chest pain. She undergoes pharmacologic stress myocardial perfusion imaging with rubidium-82 PET. The perfusion images demonstrate normal myocardial perfusion without evidence of ischemia or scar. Quantitative analysis reveals a global myocardial blood flow reserve (MBFR) of 1.4 (normal >2.0). Which of the following is the most appropriate interpretation of these findings?

A patient is administered IV regadenoson prior to stress SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging. While being placed on the camera the patient develops an acute tonic-clonic seizure and receives appropriate positioning and pharmacologic management. As part of the acute treatment the patient receives a vasodilator reversal agent. Which of the following is the best choice of reversal agent and dose for this patient?
A solid lung nodule is found when reviewing the lung fields of a vasodilator stress PET/CT. Which of the following findings requires follow-up within 3 months?

Based on study of day-to-day variation of calculated left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) by equilibrium radionuclide angiocardiography (ERNA), which of the following is correct to be attributed to nonrandom physiologic alterations?

A 61-year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia on lisinopril and pravastatin, and a 40-pack-per-year history of smoking presented with chest pressure and arm pain while working on a construction job site. His clinical exam was normal, including cardiopulmonary exam. His ECG shows sinus rhythm with non-specific ST-T wave abnormality, and he was referred for exercise myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI). He exercised 6 minutes on Bruce protocol without limitations, achieved 75% PMHR, and developed mild chest pain with normal hemodynamic response. His peak stress ECG and SPECT images are shown. What is the most appropriate next step?
Which of the following statements is the most correct regarding display of SPECT perfusion images for interpretation?

A 65-year-old female patient is referred for exercise SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging for the evaluation of chest pain with typical and atypical features and is safe to walk on the treadmill with no contraindications. She has exercised for 4 minutes on the Bruce protocol and has achieved a peak heart rate of 127 beats per minute. During the last minute she has developed the same symptoms for which she was referred and had a new horizontal ST-segment deviation of 1mm. Which of the following is the next best step?
Which acquisition modality of radionuclide blood pool ventriculography permits correlation of LVEF at different heart rates in patients with arrhythmia?
How might hyperkalemia induced T-wave peaking, conduction abnormalities, and pacemakers affect LVEF calculation with ECG-gated radionuclide angiography?

A patient with end-stage renal disease is referred for preoperative risk assessment. The patient has no symptoms to suggest CAD; however, the transplant team insists that myocardial perfusion imaging be performed. The patient does not feel capable of using a treadmill, so regadenoson SPECT is performed with normal perfusion and normal LVEF. The patient asks about risk of future CV events. Which response is the most accurate statement?
Which of the following is the best method for detecting the most hibernating myocardium?
Which of the following radiopharmaceuticals is created using a generator?
Which of the following findings on a myocardial perfusion imaging test is the strongest predictor of risk for future cardiac events and death?

A 54-year-old male with a history of tobacco abuse and no other cardiovascular risk factors, except a vague family history of heart disease, undergoes vasodilator stress SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging for exertional chest pain. His perfusion images are shown below. A recent prior unrelated chest CT was performed and showed 3-vessel diffuse calcifications. His gated images and a recent echo both showed a low-normal LVEF of 50%. He developed chest tightness during vasodilator administration and had 1mm ST-depressions in the lateral precordial leads on his stress ECG. Which of the following is the best next step?

Which of the following tests is currently considered a “gold standard” for the assessment of myocardial viability by assessing for the presence of myocardial metabolic activity and preserved cell membrane function?

A 47-year-old female with end-stage renal disease related to lupus nephritis on hemodialysis is referred for Rb-82 stress PET for progressive chest tightness and shortness of breath of 3-week duration. The image of the CT for attenuation correction is shown. What is the best next step in her evaluation?

A patient is referred for an exercise stress SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging study to assess for shortness of breath. He has a history of diabetes, hypertension, and dyslipidemia. He does not have any history of chronic kidney disease, known CAD, prior myocardial infarction, or peripheral vascular disease. He had a negative stress SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging study 3 years prior. You are considering whether to pursue a “classic” same-day low-dose rest, higher-dose stress protocol or use a low-dose stress with higher-dose rest as needed. Which of the following factors best predicts whether a low-dose stress study can be performed without the need for the resting portion?

A 64-year-old female presents to the emergency department with several hours of uncontrolled chest discomfort. She has ST-depressions noted in the inferior leads and her troponin peaks at 4. She is treated for ACS but prefers a conservative approach and proceeds with regadenoson stress myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI). She is not interested in invasive coronary angiography unless her defect location is thought to be high risk. The following perfusion images are obtained, and a polar plot is constructed. The final read highlighted the perfusion defect as shown, preserved perfusion of the apical septum, and true apex and no evidence of TID. Which of the following is the most likely location of this perfusion defect?

A 72-year-old patient with chronic coronary disease is seen in clinic for angina. The patient describes chest discomfort while playing pickleball and resolves with a few minutes of rest. Rubidium-82 PET is performed with a moderate reversible defect representing 11% of the myocardium. Ranolazine is added for the treatment of angina. Which of the following statements is true?

A 62-year-old patient with hypertension and hyperlipidemia undergoes exercise myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) for evaluation of exertional dyspnea. He exercises on a treadmill but is only able to complete 4 minutes of a standard Bruce protocol, achieving 4.5 METs due to fatigue. His peak heart rate reaches 88% of the age-predicted maximum. The perfusion images demonstrate normal myocardial perfusion without evidence of ischemia or infarction, and left ventricular function is preserved. Which of the following is the most accurate interpretation of these findings?

A 46-year-old male has new exertional angina concerning for ischemia and he is referred for stress SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging on a standard Anger camera. He has a history of known coronary disease with prior non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) and drug-eluting stent to the LAD. He has diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and obesity with BMI of 38. He has significant orthopedic limitations and is unable to exercise on the treadmill. Recent echocardiography shows a LVEF of 45% with anteroseptal wall-motion abnormality and normal wall thickness. Which of the following would be part of an optimal stress nuclear protocol for this patient?
Which of the following is a standard view for an equilibrium radionuclide angiogram (ERNA)?
Which statement is correct regarding blood pool labeling methods for RNA?

A 74-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease, insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus, and hypertension presents to clinic with progressive exertional chest tightness that resolves with rest. He is referred for exercise stress SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging. He exercised for 3 minutes on the Bruce protocol and had his typical anginal pain at peak stress. The following peak ECG and perfusion images were obtained. Which of the following factors is the most predictive of mortality in this patient?
Which of the following is an advantage of selective-stress first imaging?

A patient presents to the emergency department with a 30-minute bout of atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response with associated chest pain and then converted to normal sinus rhythm with resolution of his symptoms. He is currently asymptomatic. On physical examination he has some new leg edema and jugular venous pressure (JVP) elevation not seen on a recent visit. His first high-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hsTn) was mildly elevated and increased on the second where it then peaked. He has some T-wave inversions unchanged from a recent ECG. He is being considered for a stress radionuclide myocardial perfusion imaging study. Which of the following clinical circumstances would be a contraindication to pharmacologic stress testing?

A 65-year-old female presents for evaluation of intermittent shortness of breath with a stress SPECT MPI. She has a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and smoking. Recent pulmonary function tests showed an FEV1 82% of age predicted and a bronchodilator response of 5%. She is active and exercises on the treadmill daily. Her ECG performed on arrival in the laboratory is shown. Which of the following is the best form of stress for this patient's SPECT MPI?

A 49-year-old man with heart failure underwent an echocardiogram that showed features suggestive of cardiac amyloidosis. His Tc-99m-PYP SPECT/CT is shown below (grade 1 myocardial uptake). What is the next step in the evaluation of this patient.

A 62-year-old man undergoes pharmacologic stress Tc-99m SPECT/CT myocardial perfusion imaging for evaluation of exertional chest discomfort. Selected reconstructed attenuation-corrected perfusion images are shown in grey- and color-scale, along with the software-generated polar maps and summed scores. What is the next best step?

A 46-year-old woman with biopsy proven pulmonary sarcoidosis presents for evaluation. Echocardiogram shows normal left ventricular ejection fraction of 55% without regional wall motion abnormalities. Cardiac MRI demonstrates patchy mid-myocardial late gadolinium enhancement in the basal septum. Which of the following is the best next step in management?
In patients with suspected cardiac sarcoidosis, which of the following is correct?

A 62-year-old man with hypertension and hyperlipidemia is referred for an exercise SPECT/CT MPI to evaluate his chest pain. Results include no ischemic ECG changes after 9 minutes of exercise and normal perfusion without ischemia or infarction. A concomitant attenuation correction CT revealed three vessel coronary artery calcifications. Which of the following best describes the appropriate interpretation of the findings?

A 68-year-old man with prior anterior myocardial infarction and ischemic cardiomyopathy has a left ventricular ejection fraction of 25%. Coronary angiography demonstrates a chronic total occlusion of the left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery. He undergoes resting perfusion and F-18-FDG PET imaging to assess myocardial viability. Results are shown below. Which of the following best describes these findings?
What is the principal mechanism by which IV insulin administration helps optimize glucose uptake in normal myocardium prior to myocardial viability imaging with F-18 FDG PET?
Which PET crystal has poor energy resolution?

A 65-year-old woman with hypertension, obesity, left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) via echocardiography, and non-obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD) via coronary CT angiography (CTA) was referred for vasodilator stress flurpiridaz F-18 cardiac PET/CT due to dyspnea on exertion. The perfusion images are most consistent with which of the following findings?

A 55-year-old male with total occlusion of the LCx is referred for assessment of myocardial viability in the territory of the occlusion. An adenosine thallium-201 is performed and images are shown below. 3 mCi of thallium-201 was injected with stress. What is the next best step?

The following images are from a Tc-99m pyrophosphate scan performed on a 60-year-old male with echocardiographic features suggestive of cardiac amyloidosis. What is the next best additional testing for a diagnosis?
Which of the following factors is responsible for the decreased spatial resolution with rubidium-82 as compared to N-13 ammonia and flurpiridaz F-18 myocardial perfusion imaging?
When quantifying coronary artery calcium score (CACS) on hybrid perfusion/CT imaging, one should consider which of the following?

A 76-year-old man with severe aortic stenosis and recent biceps tendon rupture is undergoing evaluation for transcatheter aortic valve implantation. ECG shows low voltage. His echocardiogram revealed severe aortic stenosis, bi-atrial enlargement, and grade III diastolic dysfunction. A cardiac MRI demonstrated diffuse subendocardial late gadolinium enhancement. Urine and blood screen for AL amyloidosis was negative, and a PYP SPECT showed no evidence of myocardial uptake. Which of the following is the best next step in management?
Which statement most accurately reflects the value of peak stress myocardial blood flow (MBF) and myocardial flow reserve (MFR) as quantified by PET?

An 84-year-old man with carotid artery disease, hypertension, and dyslipidemia was referred for a vasodilator stress Rb-82 cardiac PET/CT due to chest pain. Based on the data below, what do you expect the most likely finding to be on invasive coronary angiography?

Which of the following rest/stress Rb-82 perfusion PET findings in a patient with no known prior CAD would be associated with the LEAST benefit of an early revascularization strategy versus a medical therapy-first strategy?
Which of the following best describes the diagnostic ability of imaging modalities for cardiac amyloidosis?

A 43-year-old man with end-stage liver disease was referred for a dobutamine stress rubidium-82 (Rb-82) cardiac PET/CT. Laboratory assessment is notable for a eGFR of 53 mL/min/1.73m2, INR of 1.6, and Hgb of 6.9 g/dL. The results in sum below are most consistent with which of the following?
Which of the following statements is true about PET/CT myocardial perfusion imaging?

A 72-year-old, obese female presents with shortness of breath and chest tightness occasionally with exertion. She has a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and diet-controlled diabetes.
